_format: Three sections, each header on its own line followed by a colon, matching the live prompt in serve.py exactly so both paths render identically: 'What AI can help with', 'What stays with you', 'Your move'.
TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT AGENT:
What AI can help with: Drafting your radio and dispatch messages, pulling plate and complaint records together before you decide, and preparing the material a new agent needs on their first week.
What stays with you: Writing the summons — which looks like the most clerical line on the page and is not, because it is an appealable record affirmed by the agent who observed the violation, and the law keeps that with a person. Patrolling and spotting a missing sign also stay with you, but for a different reason: they need someone on the street, and that one could change as technology improves.
Your move: The more the routine lookups are handled for you, the more of your day is the observation and the judgment only you can sign for.
SCHOOL SAFETY AGENT:
What AI can help with: Answering off-hours phone calls and taking messages is the one task here software could carry outright. Drafting incident write-ups, organizing entry and exit records, and preparing what you pass to police or fire are all places it can assist.
What stays with you: Apprehending or removing someone, and using force when it is necessary — that authority is vested in a person, and it is a rule question, not a capability question. Patrolling, answering an alarm, and reading a room full of students stay with you because presence is the job. Be skeptical of anything offering to write your incident reports: those are discoverable and read as your account, so a fast draft you did not really check is a risk moved onto you.
Your move: You are the person who can be asked, under oath, what happened in that hallway — and that is worth more, not less, as the routine writing gets faster.
EMERGENCY MEDICAL SPECIALIST-EMT:
What AI can help with: The handoff. Structuring what you tell the receiving hospital or the dispatcher, and coordinating with fire and police on a scene, so less of your attention goes to relaying and more goes to the patient.
What stays with you: Almost everything else, and not for sentimental reasons — assessing a patient, administering care, comforting someone who is frightened, decontaminating the bus afterward are physical acts on a person under a certification that belongs to you. One honest caveat: driving the unit is on that list because a person drives it today, and that is the one item here that could change with technology rather than with law.
Your move: Your certification and your hands are the leverage, and nothing on the horizon reaches them.
CARETAKER:
What AI can help with: The office-shaped edges. Ordering supplies against what actually gets used is the kind of thing software can simply run, and flagging a repair that needs a manager's attention is something AI can help you write up faster and more clearly.
What stays with you: Nearly all of it. The city calls this title Caretaker; the work is building cleaning and maintenance for public housing, and restrooms, floors, trash, glass, and the safe handling of cleaning chemicals all require a person physically doing them. That makes this among the least exposed work in the whole dataset — the opposite of the assumption most people arrive with.
Your move: You are the one who notices the failing system before it becomes an emergency, and the better your report, the sooner it gets fixed.
SERGEANT-:
What AI can help with: Roughly half of your listed work — briefing your command, summarizing amended law and new procedure, and keeping departmental logs and reports moving.
What stays with you: Signing off on an investigation, making a misconduct finding against a member of your command, authorizing a promotion or transfer, and directing the chain of custody over evidence. Every one of those stays with you because the law vests the act in a person — not one of them moves as models improve. That is different from the EMT down the hall, whose human-anchored work is human because it needs a body present, and could erode.
Your move: Same label on the page, opposite futures — and the half that is yours by law is the half that gets more valuable as the paperwork gets faster.
SCHOOL SECRETARY:
What AI can help with: More of this job than any other title in this tool — answering routine calls and taking messages, pulling the right file to an incoming letter, completing standard forms, making copies, and proofreading other people's work for spelling, grammar, and format. Five of the eight tasks shown here land in that bucket.
What stays with you: The front desk itself. Greeting whoever walks into a school building and judging what they need is a physical post, not a message queue — and learning each new system as it arrives is something that attaches to you, not to the software. Drafting routine replies stays partly yours too, because those letters go out over the school's name and are read as the school's position.
Your move: Worth saying plainly — this is the most exposed title we analyzed, and it is a school office, not a factory floor. The leverage is that the work only you can do is the judgment at the counter, and every hour the copying and proofreading gives back is an hour spent there.
TEACHER- PER SESSION:
What AI can help with: Nothing, honestly — because this is not a job. It is how the Department of Education pays teachers hourly for after-school and summer work, and the people under it are overwhelmingly already counted under TEACHER.
What stays with you: Your actual teaching title, which is where this question belongs. The tell is on this page: the median annual salary is null, because almost nobody is paid annually under this line.
Your move: We would rather report these 78,618 rows as a documented exclusion than invent a job to put a number on — so look up the title you actually hold.
ELECTION WORKER:
What AI can help with: Nothing we can honestly tell you, because this is a civic stipend role rather than an occupation. The city's own payroll keeps poll workers in a separate agency of 36,732 rows, apart from the 1,027 people who staff the Board of Elections year-round.
What stays with you: There are zero salaried rows here, so there is no career this analysis could describe. Coding it as a job would launder a stipend into an occupation and then attach an AI score to it.
Your move: The useful question for this work is about the election process itself, not about anyone's career exposure — so we stop rather than guess.
STUDENT AIDE:
What AI can help with: We cannot say, and that is the finding. This is a hiring category — students placed across many different city agencies doing many different things under one payroll label.
What stays with you: There is no single set of tasks to analyze here, so a job-level answer would be an average across work that has nothing in common.
Your move: Ask what your specific placement actually involves — the payroll file does not record it, and naming that gap is more useful to you than a confident number.
JOB TRAINING PARTICIPANT:
What AI can help with: Nothing here, because the title names the program you are enrolled in, not the work you do. The payroll data shows it plainly: 18 salaried rows out of 4,021.
What stays with you: There is no occupation on this line to describe, so there is nothing honest to say about AI exposure for it. That is a finding about how the city classifies people, not a gap in our data.
Your move: The meaningful analysis attaches to the job the training leads to — that is where this tool should point you next.
F/T SCHOOL AIDE:
What AI can help with: We are not going to guess, and this one is different from the titles we skip — these are 9,217 people doing real jobs.
What stays with you: The problem is that the work sits in three completely different occupational families — education support, office and clerical, and food service — depending on the school assignment, and no single occupation code spans them. Picking one would misclassify most of the people under the title.
Your move: Resolving this needs Department of Education school-assignment data, which is not in the payroll file — so the honest answer today is that the title is real and the tasks are not yet knowable.
COLLEGE ASSISTANT:
What AI can help with: Not answerable yet, and the reason is worth knowing. This one title covers clerical, tutoring, laboratory, and library assignments across CUNY's community colleges — genuinely different occupations sharing one payroll label.
What stays with you: Any single occupation code would describe a minority of the people in it, so a task-level analysis would be confidently wrong rather than usefully approximate. This population is also larger than people assume: CUNY's community colleges are city-funded and appear in this payroll file under their own campus names.
Your move: Getting a real answer means splitting the title by assignment first — work we have not done, rather than work we are hiding.
CITY SEASONAL AIDE:
What AI can help with: Nothing, and this is the most important screen in the tool. City Seasonal Aide is a hiring category, not a job — in FY2025 only 17 of its 2,414 payroll rows carry an annual salary.
What stays with you: The people under this title are doing genuinely different work in different agencies. Any tool that hands you a single risk number here is quietly averaging a lifeguard, a parks crew member, and an office temp into one figure that is wrong for every one of them.
Your move: What you need first is the work described accurately — which tasks, in which agency — before anyone says a word about automation. Our eval fails the build if we ever fill this in with a guess.
